🗳️💻 The technology behind your vote, explained

📱 Checking you in: at every voting station, a Voter Management Device (VMD) checks you off the voters' roll. This year the IEC added barcode scanners to speed up ID checks. The IEC said the devices worked well on 4 November.

📶 No signal? No problem: the devices store voter information on the device and sync when the network comes back, so rural stations keep working.

📊 From station to scoreboard: once ballots are counted by hand at the station, party agents sign the results slip. The results are then sent to the national results centre in Midrand. The IEC said it improved this system after 2024, when the results board went blank for about two hours.

🔍 Checks before the final word: the IEC dealt with 197 objections and ordered recounts in five wards before declaring. The MK Party says system failures affected eThekwini and wants those results frozen. That is its claim, which the IEC must answer.

Why it matters for your pocket: trusted results mean stable councils, and stable councils pass budgets on time.
